endpoint.cursor: opaque per-section next_cursor; cursor page takes precedence over page query; registry membership/status change returns409 requiring restart
endpoint.status: partial takes precedence over stale, then ok
endpoint.count_semantics: projects count is registry size; attention/working and section totals/pages null when global coverage is incomplete; true empty known scope is0
endpoint.working_semantics: file doing summaries match existing backlog count semantics; state_provisional=true and lifecycle/activity=null until canonical projection exists; no execution start inferred from doing
endpoint.activity_source: existing notification_events journal only, not entire runtime/activity ledger
endpoint.pagination: all known items in a loaded batch, then next8-project batch; coverage reports current batch, not cumulative history
endpoint.retry: loading source job500ms; pending canonical projection5000ms; complete/stale but not pending0; client uses finite active-screen polling

bounds.cold_request: registry metadata only; starts bounded background pure-read job and returns loading partial without waiting for catalog IO
limitations: ManagedProjects still enumerates registered project metadata O(P); no claim of strict wall-time bound for registry filesystem metadata.
Each chosen project can require a complete existing CachedCatalog walk in the background. HTTP does not wait; per-project scan runtime/task count is not individually capped.
No separate index or canonical control plane is created. Cache and source query costs are reused; aggregate summary memory follows the tasks/events in up to8 cached batches.
For >8 projects, totals stay globally unknown in each window; cursors provide exhaustive access rather than pretending the window is a complete global sum.
